pages.text: "I'll crack the eggs!" Coco, in a red headscarf, picked up an egg at the dough table. Snow lay outside. In the kitchen, it was egg-bread day. "I'll put in a nice round yolk!"
Coco hit the egg against the bowl. Crack! Shell pieces tumbled in, and the yolk burst into a yellow puddle. "Huh? Why did that happen?" Coco's shoulders sank.
Coco tried to pick out the shells with a paw, but they kept slipping away. Coco pushed the bowl aside and lay across the table. "I can't do it... I won't." Their tail drooped.
Bakery Mom, with flour on her arms, came beside Coco. "My first eggs were full of shell too. Shell fell in? Tap again!" Mom placed a new egg in Coco's paw.
"Here's how. Not hard—just a gentle tap on the table edge." Mom showed Coco. "Once it cracks, pull it open with both paws." Coco's ears perked up.
Coco tapped the egg gently on the edge. A crack appeared. Both paws pulled it open. Plop! The yolk landed in the bowl. Just one bit of shell. "Only one piece!" Coco called. Shell fell in? Tap again!
Coco tightened the scarf knot with both paws and picked up a fresh egg. Gentle tap, pull open. Plop! A round yolk! No shell at all! "I did it! A round yolk!" Coco hopped.
As Mr. Pig set down a flour sack, he saw three bowls. Lots of shell, one bit of shell, then a round yolk. "Ha ha! Three tries, and you did it!" He clapped.
When Coco picked up an egg, they looked for the table edge first. "One, it's okay if it doesn't work! Two, ask how! Three, shell fell in? Tap again!" Coco called, "Next time I'll crack ten!"
By the oven, Mom gave Coco a sideways hug. The first egg was full of shell, but the third had a round yolk. The egg bread puffed up golden. Coco called, "Shell fell in? Tap again!"
